original_description: Use this skill whenever anyone worries that writing might come across as AI-generated, whether it's their own or someone else's, or wants to understand an AI checker's verdict. Examples: a writer who fears readers will think their newsletter, blog, essay, cover letter, or post came from a bot because of habits like heavy em dash use, words like "delve", or tidy three-part lists; a student with a Turnitin AI score or GPTZero result asking what it means and why passages were flagged; a teacher, editor, or reviewer suspicious of a submission; a draft to check for "ChatGPT voice" before publishing or sending; anyone asking to de-slop or humanize text. It flags passages that read as LLM output, explains why, reads detector reports, and revises without flattening voice. Use it even when the user names only one tell, and to check your own drafts. Skip it for plain proofreading, shortening, translating, punch-up edits where AI-sounding isn't the worry, plagiarism or similarity reports, and fiction.
